289.sol: Vernalisation refers specially to the promotion of flowering by exposure to a period of low temperature. 4981.subject: Chemistry
4981.text: The correct order of the metallic character of the elements Be , Al , Na , K is
4981.sol: Metallic character decreases as we move across a period in the periodic table from left to right. This occurs as atoms more readily accept electrons to fill a valence shell than lose them to remove the unfilled shell. Metallic character increases as we move down an element group in the periodic table. Potassium belongs to 4th period, sodium and aluminium belong to 3rd period, beryllium belongs to 2nd period in the periodic table. Hence, their correct metallic character is K > Na > Al > Be .

71387.subject: Biology
71387.text: Girl of normal vision whose father was colorblind marries a man of normal vision whose father was also colourblind. The sons of this marriage would be
71387.sol: Color blindness is an X-linked recessive trait. Let X^C be the normal allele and X^c be the colorblind allele. The girl has normal vision but her father was colorblind ( X^c Y ). She must have inherited the X^c chromosome from her father, making her genotype X^C X^c (carrier). The man has normal vision, so his genotype is X^C Y . The fact that his father was colorblind does not affect his genotype, as he inherits the Y chromosome from his father. When they marry ( X^C X^c X^C Y ), the sons inherit the Y chromosome

71399.subject: Biology
71399.text: The process of sexual reproduction in animals involves
options: mitosis only and fusion of gametes to form a diploid zygote
meiosis and fusion gametes to form diploid zygote
71399.sol: Sexual reproduction in animals involves the production of haploid gametes from diploid germ cells through the process of meiosis. These haploid male and female gametes then fuse during fertilization to form a diploid zygote, which subsequently develops into a new organism. Therefore, the process essentially involves both meiosis and the fusion of gametes to form a diploid zygote. Answer: meiosis and fusion gametes to form diploid zygote

79609.sol: Glycocalyx is a gelatinous polysaccharide and/or polypeptide covering present in the cell envelop in bacteria. When it occurs in the form of a loose sheath, it is known as a slime layer. 80656.sol: Active transport occurs with the help of energy, usually against concentration gradient. For this, cell membrane possesses carriers and gated channels. 84323.sol: Gastric glands are numerous microscopic tubular glands formed by the epithelium of stomach. Therefore, the fraction of mass remaining ( N ) is 1 - 7 8 = 1 8 . The total time required is the number of half-lives multiplied by the half-life period: t = n t_ 1/2 t = 3 30 days

116550.text: According to IUPAC, how are transition metals defined?
116550.sol: According to IUPAC, transition metals are defined as metals which have incomplete d subshell either in neutral atom or in their ions, as mentioned in the paragraph.

116551.subject: Chemistry
116551.text: What type of molecules or ions can bind to metal ions to form complex species?
116551.sol: The paragraph mentions that metal ions can bind to anions or neutral molecules to form complex species.

116615.subject: Chemistry
116615.text: What causes the increase in ionization enthalpy along each series of transition elements from left to right?
options: An increase in the number of d electrons
An increase in the number of s electrons
An increase in the number of p electrons
116615.sol: The increase in ionization enthalpy along each series of transition elements is due to an increase in nuclear charge.

116652.subject: Chemistry
116652.text: What effect does the loss of exchange energy have on ionization enthalpy?
options: It has no effect on ionization enthalpy
116652.sol: The loss of exchange energy increases the stability, making ionization more difficult.

118240.subject: Chemistry

118555.subject: Chemistry
118555.text: Which of the following reagents is used to initiate the Grignard reaction?
118555.sol: Magnesium metal is typically used to initiate the Grignard reaction.

119029.subject: Chemistry

119029.sol: A positive Tollens' test for an aldehyde is indicated by the formation of a bright silver mirror.

120222.subject: Chemistry
120222.text: What is the result of the antibiotic revolution in terms of life expectancy?
options: Life expectancy has remained the same
120222.sol: The antibiotic revolution has almost doubled life expectancy.

120590.subject: Chemistry
120590.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of vitamins?
options: They are required in large quantities.
120590.sol: Vitamins are required in small quantities, not large quantities, to maintain health and prevent deficiency diseases.

120849.subject: Chemistry
120849.text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: Maltose has two α - D - glucose units linked at C 1 and C 4 and is a reducing sugar. Statement II: Maltose has two monosaccharides: α - D -glucose and β - D -glucose linked at C 1 and C 6 and it is a non-reducing sugar. options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
120849.sol: Maltose is composed of two α - D -glucose units in which C - 1 of one glucose is linked to C - 4 of another glucose unit. As there is a free aldehydic group on one of the components of the disaccharides,It is a reducing sugar.

121033.subject: Chemistry
121033.text: Two alleles of the same gene possess chemical variation of
121033.sol: Alleles are slightly different forms of the same gene which are found at a particular place or locus on homologous chromosomes and control the same character. Two alleles of the same gene possess chemical variation of DNA.

121467.subject: Botany

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
121467.sol: Phycomycetes members can reproduce asexually and form zoospores (motile) or aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in sporangium.

122012.subject: Botany
122012.text: What is an example of isogamy?
122012.sol: Algae is an example of isogamy.

122211.subject: Botany
122211.sol: Ctenophores are exclusively marine organisms that have radially symmetrical body structure. Ctenophores have eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help them in locomotion.Ctenophores have both intracellular and extracellular digestion. Bioluminescence, the property of emitting light, is well-marked in ctenophores . Sexes are not separate. Reproduction takes place only by sexual means. Fertilisation is external with indirect development.

122522.subject: Botany
122522.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry whereas their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. Reason (R): Echinoderms possess a water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer fro
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
122522.sol: Assertion (A) is true. Echinoderms are unique in their symmetry; adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. Reason (R) is also true. The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of a water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration. However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The developmental shift in symmetry is not caused by the presence of the water vascular system. Therefore, both Assertion (A) a

122531.subject: Botany
122531.text: An animal is observed to have bilateral symmetry and three embryonic germ layers. However, it completely lacks any cavity between the body wall and the gut. Based on these characteristics, to which of the following phyla does this animal belong?
122531.sol: The animal described is bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic (having three embryonic germ layers), and acoelomate (lacking a body cavity between the body wall and the gut). According to NCERT, members of the phylum Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, and acoelomate animals. Aschelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic, but they are pseudocoelomates. Ctenophora are radially symmetrical and diploblastic. Annelida are bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic, but t

122581.subject: Botany
122581.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Scoliodon and Carcharodon have to swim constantly to avoid sinking. Reason (R): They belong to class Chondrichthyes, which lack an air bladder. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
122581.sol: Assertion (A) is correct. Scoliodon (Dog fish) and Carcharodon (Great white shark) are cartilaginous fishes that must swim constantly to avoid sinking. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the correct explanation for (A). Members of the class Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder, which is a buoyancy-regulating organ. Due to the absence of this organ, they are forced to swim continuously to maintain their position in the water column and avoid sinking. Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct exp

122954.subject: Botany
122954.text: The mature seeds of plants such as gram and peas, possess no endosperm, because
options: There is no double fertilization in them
Endosperm is not formed in them
Endosperm gets used up by the developing embryo during seed development.
122954.sol: The mature seeds of plants such as gram and peas, possess no endosperm, because endosperm gets used up by the developing embryo during seed development.

123304.subject: Botany
123304.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Bulliform cells prevent water loss Reason: The parallel venation in monocot leaves is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
123304.sol: When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

123419.subject: Botany
123419.text: Read the following statements regarding the vascular cambium in a dicot stem: (A) Intrafascicular cambium is present between primary xylem and primary phloem. (B) Interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of endodermal cells. (C) The continuous cambial ring is partly primary and partly secondary in origin. (D) Interfascicular cambium is an example of a primary meristem. How many of the above statemen
123419.sol: Statement (A) is correct as the cambium present inside the vascular bundle, between primary xylem and primary phloem, is the intrafascicular cambium. Statement (B) is incorrect because interfascicular cambium is formed by the dedifferentiation of medullary ray cells, not endodermal cells. Statement (C) is correct because the continuous cambial ring is formed by both intrafascicular cambium (which is primary in origin) and interfascicular cambium (which is secondary in origin). Statement (D) is incorrect because int

123663.subject: Botany
123663.text: What happens during the leptotene stage of meiosis?
options: Chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope
Chromosomes are no longer visible under the light microscope
123663.sol: Prophase I: Prophase of the first meiotic division is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of mitosis. It has been further subdivided into the following five phases based on chromosomal behaviour, i.e., Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. During leptotene stage the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope. The compaction of chromosomes continues throughout leptotene. This is followed by the second stage of prophase I called zygotene.

123678.subject: Botany
123678.text: What is the name given to the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes during pachytene stage?
123678.sol: During this stage, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosomes becomes distinct and clearly appears as tetrads. This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is also an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase.

123956.subject: Botany
123956.text: Which of the following organisms is composed of a single cell?
123956.sol: All organisms are composed of cells. Some are composed of a single cell and are called unicellular organisms while others, like us, composed of many cells, are called multicellular organisms.

123981.subject: Botany
123981.text: How does the thickness of the glycocalyx vary among different bacteria?
options: It varies and can be thick or thin
It is the same thickness in all bacteria
123981.sol: Glycocalyx differs in composition and thickness among different bacteria. It could be a loose sheath called the slime layer in some, while in others it may be thick and tough, called the capsule . The cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.

124337.subject: Botany
124337.text: The stroma of a chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. Which of the following correctly represents the type of genetic material and ribosomes present in the chloroplast stroma?
124337.sol: The stroma of the chloroplast contains its own genetic machinery and protein-synthesizing apparatus. According to NCERT, the chloroplast stroma contains small, double-stranded circular DNA molecules. Additionally, the ribosomes present in the chloroplasts are of the 70S type, which are smaller than the 80S ribosomes found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotes. Thus, the correct combination is circular double-stranded DNA and 70S ribosomes. Answer: Circular double-stranded DNA and 70S ribosomes

124446.subject: Botany
124446.text: Spindle fibre is made up of
124446.sol: 'Tubulin' is a cytoskeletal globular protein that polymerizes to form microtubules. It plays a motile and contractile role in cell structure and cell division. During cell division, the microtubules radiate from each end of the cell form a basket like arrangement (the spindle) which helps in the movement of chromosomes to poles. The principal protein of cilia and flagella is also tubulin. Microtubules play a key role in the movement of cilia and flagella. Intermediate filaments are tough rope-like bundles or protei

124810.subject: Botany
124810.text: Assertion : Cytokinins increases shelf life of fruits and vegetables. Reason : Cytokinins induce cell division.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
124810.sol: Application of cytokinins to marketed vegetables can keep them fresh for several days. Shelf life of cut shoots and flowers is prolonged by employing the hormone cytokinin. The reason is that the cytokinin increases retention of chlorophyll and delayed senescence in leaves. Cytokinin as the name suggests, is essential for cell division or cytokinesis. It promotes cell division along with auxin by controlling the activity of cyclin dependent kinases.

124982.subject: Botany
124982.text: What is the product of the condensation of the acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid and water?
124982.sol: The TCA cycle starts with the condensation of acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid (OAA) and water to yield citric acid (Figure 12.3). The reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme citrate synthase and a molecule of CoA is released. Citrate is then isomerized to isocitrate.

125509.subject: Botany
125509.text: Identify and name the labelled structures respectively.

125833.subject: Botany
125833.text: What form of pollen products is available in western countries?
125833.sol: Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people often leading to chronic respiratory disorders– asthma, bronchitis, etc. It may be mentioned that Parthenium or carrot grass that came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat, has become ubiquitous in occurrence and causes pollen allergy. Pollen grains are rich in nutrients. It has become a fashion in recent years to use pollen tablets as food supplements. In western countries, a large number of pollen products in

126334.subject: Botany
126334.text: Plants of which one of the following groups of genera are pollinated by the same agency?
126334.sol: Pollination by birds is called ornithophily, eg. humming birds, honey eaters, sumbirds etc. are sensitive to colours and have powerful vision. Plants like Bombax, Butea, etc are ornithophilous plants. There flowers are characterised by tubular, cup shaped corolla, bright colour to attract insect, excess of nectar and pollens. They are generally odourless. Bauhinia is mostly visited by hummingbirds and their propagules are dispersed by birds.

126393.subject: Botany
126393.text: Which of the following is the most resistant material in pollen grain?
126393.sol: Sporopollenin is most resistant chemical substance in pollen grains wall.

126491.subject: Botany
126491.text: What is an active site in an enzyme?
options: The pocket or crevice into which the substrate fits
126491.sol: The backbone of the protein chain folds upon itself, the chain criss-crosses itself and hence, many crevices or pockets are made. One such pocket is the ‘active site’. An active site of an enzyme is a crevice or pocket into which the substrate fits. Thus enzymes, through their active site, catalyse reactions at a high rate.

126757.subject: Botany
126757.text: Read the following statements regarding lipids: Statement I: The R group in a fatty acid could be a methyl, ethyl or higher number of - CH ₂ groups (1 carbon to 19 carbons). Statement II: Palmitic acid has 16 carbons excluding the carboxyl carbon. Statement III: Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon. Statement IV: Oils have higher melting points than fats and hence remain as oil in winter
126757.sol: Statement I is correct; the R group in fatty acids can range from 1 to 19 carbons. Statement II is incorrect; palmitic acid has 16 carbons including the carboxyl carbon, not excluding it. Statement III is correct; arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon. Statement IV is incorrect; oils have lower melting points (e.g., gingelly oil) compared to fats, which is why they remain liquid in winter. Thus, exactly two statements (I and III) are correct. Answer: Only two

127863.subject: Botany
127863.text: From which of the following plant is a medicine for respiratory disorders obtained?
127863.sol: Ephidrine is obtained from several species of Ephedra of family-Ephideraceae. It is used in the treatment of respiratory disorders like cold, asthma, bronchial congestion.

128011.subject: Zoology
128011.text: Choose the correct option after carefully reading the statement: (I) The Body of a frog is divided into the head, neck and trunk. (II) Eyes are bulged. (III) The forelimbs alone help in swimming and walking. (IV) Feet have webbed digits. (V) Above the mouth, a nostril is present.
options: True II, IV; False I, III, V
True I, II, IV, V; False III
True I, II, V; False III, IV
True I,II; False IV, III, V
128011.sol: Body of a frog is divisible into its head and trunk. A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of the eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than forelimbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in

128945.subject: Zoology
options: Due to conditions that affect the blood flow
Due to the state of heart when it is pumping blood effectively
Due to congestion of the lungs
128945.sol: It is also called ‘angina pectoris’. A symptom of acute chest pain appears when no enough oxygen is reaching the heart muscle . Angina can occur in men and women of any age but it is more common among the middle-aged and elderly. It occurs due to conditions that affect the blood flow..

129860.subject: Zoology
129860.text: What is the first layer of the diffusion membrane made of?
129860.sol: The gradient is present for CO2 in the opposite direction, i.e., from tissues to blood and blood to alveoli. As the solubility of CO2 is 20-25 times higher than that of O2, the amount of CO2 that can diffuse through the diffusion membrane per unit difference in partial pressure is much higher compared to that of O2 . The diffusion membrane is made up of three major layers namely, the thin squamous epithelium of alveoli, the endothelium of alveolar capillaries and the basement substance (composed of a thin basement

129959.subject: Zoology
129959.text: What conditions shift the graph to the right?
129959.sol: This curve is called the Oxygen dissociation curve (Figure 17.5) and is highly useful in studying the effect of factors like , H+ concentration, etc., on binding of O2 with haemoglobin. In the alveoli, where there is high , low , lesser H+ concentration and lower temperature, the factors are all favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin, whereas in the tissues, where low , high , high H+ concentration and higher temperature exist, the conditions are favourable for dissociation of oxygen from the oxyhaemoglobin

129980.subject: Zoology
129980.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases Reason: Solubility of gases affect the rate of diffusion
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
129980.sol: Alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases. Exchange of gases also occur between blood and tissues. O2 and CO2 are exchanged in these sites by simple diffusion mainly based on pressure/concentration gradient.

130089.subject: Zoology
130089.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During normal expiration, air moves out of the lungs because intrapulmonary pressure becomes slightly higher than atmospheric pressure. Reason (R): Relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles decreases the thoracic volume, which leads to an increase in intrapulmonary pressure. In t
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
130089.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the movement of air into or out of the lungs is driven by pressure gradients. For expiration to occur, the pressure inside the lungs (intrapulmonary pressure) must be higher than the atmospheric pressure, forcing air outward. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the accurate physiological mechanism for this pressure change. Normal expiration is a passive process initiated by the relaxation of the primary inspiratory muscles (the diaphragm and external intercostals). This relaxati

130399.subject: Zoology
130399.text: Skeletal Muscle Component Composition A. A-band 1. Contains only actin filaments B. I-band 2. Contains both actin and myosin filaments C. H-zone 3 .Contains only myosin filaments D. Z-line 4. Composed of proteins that anchor actin filaments
130399.sol: A-band: The dark band that contains both actin and myosin filaments. I-band: The light band that contains only actin filaments. H-zone: The central part of the A-band that contains only myosin filaments. Z-line: A structure composed of proteins that anchors the actin filaments and defines the boundaries of a sarcomere.

130543.subject: Zoology
130543.text: Which mediums are used by governmental and non-governmental agencies to create awareness about reproduction-related aspects?
130543.sol: With the help of audio-visual and the print-media governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among the people about reproduction-related aspects. Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the above information. Introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related

130673.subject: Zoology
130673.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Coitus interruptus is a type of natural contraceptive Reason: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
130673.sol: Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination.

130814.subject: Zoology
130814.text: 'Treponema pallidum' pathogen is a cause of
130814.sol: Syphilis is a Sexually Transmitted Disease (STD) which is caused by Treponema pallidum bacteria.

131000.subject: Zoology

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion

132878.sol: Lobe fish evolved into the first amphibians that lived on both land and water.

132979.subject: Zoology
132979.text: After about how many years of formation of earth, life appeared on this planet?
132979.sol: Life took approximately 500 million ( 5   x   10 8 ) years to appear after the formation of the earth. Thus life is thought to be evolved almost 4 billion ( 4 x 10 9 ) years back from now, as the earth was formed 4 . 5 billion ( 4 . 5 x 10 9 ) years ago.

133253.subject: Zoology
133253.text: What is the function of the spleen in the human body regarding erythrocytes?
options: Acts as a filter of erythrocytes
Acts as a storage of erythrocytes
133253.sol: The primary lymphoid organs in the human body are the bone marrow and thymus, where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.The thymus is quite large at the time of birth but keeps reducing in size with age. By the time puberty is attained, it reduces to a very small size. The spleen mainly contains lymphocytes and phagocytes. It acts as a filter of the blood by trapping blood-borne microorganisms. It also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes. Both bone marrow and thymus provide micro

133987.subject: Zoology
133987.sol: Cyclosporin-A is a bioactive molecule, which is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ transplantation. It is obtained through fermentative activity of fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

134600.subject: Zoology
134600.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The matrix used in gel electrophoresis should have controllable pore size. Reason: Agarose concentration can be changed to change pore sizes.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134600.sol: Nowadays the most commonly used matrix is agarose which is a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds. The DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel. Hence, the smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves.

134925.subject: Zoology
134925.text: Thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR was isolated from :
134925.sol: Option (3) is the answer, because Thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) used in PCR was isolated from a bacterium Thermus aquaticus. Option (1) is not the answer as Agrobacterium tumifaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants. Option (2) is not the answer as, specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis and incorporated into the several crop plants for the development of pest resistant crops. E. Coli was used as a host by Eli lily to produce human insulin.

135307.subject: Zoology
135307.text: Evolutionary Relationship Consequences A. Co-evolution of Fig and Wasp 1. Orchid Fails to Attract Bee B. Sexual Deceit in Orchid 2. Wasp Pollinates Fig C. Lack of Co-evolution 3. Orchid Attracts Bee D. Mutualism Breakdown 4. Lack of Mutual Benefits
135307.sol: Co-evolution between fig trees and wasps results in successful pollination. Sexual deceit in orchids ensures bee attraction. A lack of co-evolution can lead to failure in attracting pollinators. Breakdown of mutualism results in a lack of mutual benefits.

69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5b136.subject: Biology
69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5b136.text: In a pond ecosystem, benthos means
options: Primary consumers in the depth of a pond
69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5b136.sol: Benthos are the organisms that are found at the nethermost of stream bodies such as streams, rivers, and lakes. In 1891, the term Benthos was coined by Haeckel. Benthos are depending on the organic matter. - The ponds and lakes are motionless or immobile freshwaters. In general, the ponds are thinner with depth less than 2 meters. - In an ecosystem of pond or lake benthos (which are also known as the bottom dwellers) comprises snails, clams, mussels, crabs, prawns, etc. - The benthos lives deep in any water resourc

69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5af8e.subject: Botany
69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5af8e.text: The function of companion cells is to
options: Provide energy to sieve elements for active transport
Load sucrose into sieve elements by passive transport
Load sucrose into sieve elements by active transport
69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5af8e.sol: Companion cells move sugar and amino acids into and out of the sieve elements. In "source" tissue such as the leaf, companion cells use transmembrane proteins to take up sugar and amino acids by active transport. Movement of sugars in the phloem begins at the source, where sugars are loaded (actively transported) into a sieve tube. Loading sets up a water potential gradient that facilitates the movement of sugar.

6a13e469688ac6d0667aad6d.subject: Biology
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad6d.text: Which of the following techniques involves the direct introduction of recombinant DNA into the nucleus of an animal cell?
6a13e469688ac6d0667aad6d.sol: In the micro-injection technique, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell. Biolistics or gene gun method is primarily used to introduce DNA into plant cells. The heat shock method is used to make bacterial cells competent to take up recombinant DNA. Disarmed Agrobacterium vectors are used to deliver genes of interest into plant cells. Answer: Micro-injection

6a13e46b688ac6d0667aada5.subject: Biology
6a13e46b688ac6d0667aada5.text: In the human brain, the regions responsible for complex functions like intersensory associations, memory, and communication are known as:
6a13e46b688ac6d0667aada5.sol: The cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas, and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions are called association areas. Association areas are responsible for complex functions like intersensory associations, memory, and communication. Answer: Association areas

96443.text: Which of these Eltonian pyramids are correctly described?
options: Pyramid of numbers- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of biomass- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of energy-
Pyramid of numbers- always erect, Pyramid of biomass- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of energy- may be erec

96443.sol: Energy keeps on decreasing in successive trophic levels. Hence, producers will have maximum energy while top carnivore will have the least energy. Hence, the pyramid of energy is always erect and never inverted. Pyramids of numbers and biomass may be upright or inverted.

96862.subject: Botany
96862.text: Which of these statements regarding modified roots and stem is incorrect?
options: In Asparagus, adventitious root is modified for food storage
Prop roots are for mechanical support
Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and colocasia are modified for photosynthesis
Onion is an example of modified shoot
96862.sol: Asparagus has fasciculated roots that arise in a bunch from a lower node of the stem and become fleshy for the storage of food. It is a type of modified adventitious root. Underground stems of potato (tuber), ginger and turmeric (rhizome), zaminkand and colocasia (corm) are used for food storage and vegetative propagation. Onion is a modified underground stem called the bulb. This stem is reduced and has a disc-like structure and surrounds with numerous fleshly scaly leaves.

96876.sol: In vexillary aestivation, the five petals are arranged in a descending imbricate manner and are observed in Fabaceae. Perianth is also called tepal. The fused sepals and petals are called as perianth and are observed in Liliaceae. False septum, also called replum which divides the unilocular ovary into bilocular and bilocular ovary into tetralocular ovary, is observed in mustard plant. Persistent sepals are observed in the Solanaceae family.

6a7a1ff8399a98ce6efc1d10.sol: In Group 14, the stability of the +4 oxidation state decreases down the group due to the inert pair effect.
